notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment No. 64 &
notes: Aminu Bello gave a presentation outlining the proposed development, including the site context and the planning amendments being requested. He then responded to questions of Council.

Heather Price, Vice President, GSP Group gave presentation offering further details for the proposal, including the unit breakdown and building renderings. She then responded to questions of Council. Aminu Bello also responded to questions of Council.

Phil Elsworthy, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation describing some of the historical importance of the site, including the Indigenous significance of the Public Square. Aminu Bello responded to questions of Council.

Ashwin Annamalai, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the importance of leveraging the location of the ION light rail, and things to keep in mind with a tall building, such as the number of elevators and whether the fire department is equipped to handle it. Aminu Bello responded to questions of Council.

June Canete, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the shadow studies submitted, and how the lack of sunlight will impact residents, as well as the reflections from the building. June Canete also spoke about the traffic studies, and the general size of the building. June Canete then responded to questions of Council. Aminu Bello also responded to questions of Council.

Nabil Fahel, Resident of Waterloo spoke in support of the proposal, citing the vibrancy it will bring to the Public Square, and the need for more housing. Nabil Fahel then responded to questions of Council.
Craig Sloss, Resident of Waterloo spoke about living in the area, and in support of the development, especially during the housing crisis.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: Notice of Motion
notes: Mayor McCabe – Ontario Regulation 391/2, Blue Box Motion Motion to be tabled September 22, 2025 for Council consideration September 29, 2025.

WHEREAS under Ontario Regulation 391/2, Blue Box producers are fully accountable and financially responsible for their products and packaging once they reach their end of life and are disposed of for ‘eligible’ sources only; and

WHEREAS ‘ineligible’ sources, which producers are not responsible for, include business improvement areas, places of worship, daycares, camp grounds, public facing and internal areas of municipal-owned buildings, and not-for-profit organizations, such as shelters and food banks; and WHEREAS should a municipality continue to provide services to the ‘ineligible’ sources, the municipality will be required to oversee the collection, transportation, and processing of the recycling, assuming 100% of the costs; and

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT City of Waterloo Council request that the province amend Ontario Regulation 391/21, Blue Box so that producers are responsible for the end-of-life management of recycling products from all sources as stated above;
AND THAT Council request the support of all Ontario Municipalities;

AND THAT this resolution be forwarded to the Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, the Honourable Todd McCarthy, Minister of the Environment, Conservation and Parks, the Honourable Mike Harris, Minister of Natural Resources, the Honourable Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, to local and area MPPs, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), the Association of Municipal Managers, Clerks and Treasurers of Ontario (AMCTO), and to the Region of Waterloo and local area municipalities.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Freeman asked a question for staff to take away regarding the status of the Wissler Road reconstruction. In the Old Abbey subdivision, there are only two roads in and out: Old Abbey Road and Wissler Road. Wissler Road has been closed for two months now, when it was supposed to be closed for two weeks. Councillor Freeman asked staff to follow up with the developer.

Councillor Freeman was also wondering how staff allocate how many picnic tables are available in public parks. There are 88 new units on Kingscourt Drive, and the City has made investments in the park, including paving the walkways, but there is only one picnic table. The park is being used as a gathering place for the community, and the neighbourhood association is also trying to make space and has asked for more picnic tables. Councillor Freeman asked if staff could take this away.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Wright wanted to acknowledge Lumen on Saturday, September 20. She offered her thanks to City staff and sponsors that help make Lumen possible. There were a lot of people enjoying it, and it was a clear night with perfect weather. It was really fun to navigate the different stations. There were activities set up in Waterloo Park, the Public Square, the Museum Lot, and outside City Hall.

Councillor Vasic mentioned that the City’s Neighbourhood Team has been helping neighbourhoods name their areas, which is a great way to build cohesion and a sense of community. She wanted to thank the Team for doing two of these events in Ward 5 at Lexington and Auburn Parks with movies. A lot of people came out, including the Mayor.
Councillor Vasic also mentioned that Princess Cinemas had their 40th Anniversary Block Party last Thursday, September 18. Jane Bond had their patio open, which was great.

The theatre showed Casablanca in the morning inside the theatre, and Stop Making Sense later in the day. She congratulated Princess for 40 years, and to the BIA and City staff for helping to make it happen with the closure of Princess Street.

Councillor Freeman also wanted to highlight the Neighbourhoods team for the amazing job they did supporting the Foxhunt Neighbourhood Association. They held the party in the park on Sunday, September 21 and lucked out on the weather, as the event was held before the storm and flooding Sunday night. The Kid Chocolatier was there, and orders can be placed now for Halloween chocolates.

Councillor Roach mentioned that this Thursday, September 25, the Lakeshore South Community Association is hosting an open house at the Albert McCormick Community Centre at 6:30 p.m. It’s to give the community an opportunity to get more information about the new hospital being built near the University of Waterloo. They’re looking for how it’s going to affect the community regarding transportation, noise, housing, and community character. Councillor Roach wanted to thank Adam Lauder for helping him get some information pulled together ahead of the open house.

Mayor McCabe mentioned that yesterday afternoon, September 21, was the 2025 Awards of Excellence held by the Congress of Black Women of Canada and the Caribbean Canadian Association of Waterloo Region. They celebrated 22 students at different points in their educational career for their achievements in the community.
Mayor McCabe wanted to congratulate all the recipients, and thanked the organizations and their volunteers for continuing to find ways to support Black youth in our community.
Councillor Freeman invited Council and the Corporate Management Team to do a brief round table to introduce themselves to the University of Waterloo students that came out.
